answer: According to NIST AI RMF 1.0, privacy-enhancing techniques (PETs) for AI, as well as data minimizing methods such as de-identification and aggregation for certain model outputs, can support the design for privacy-enhanced AI systems. However, under certain conditions such as data sparsity, these privacy-enhancing techniques can result in a loss in accuracy. This loss in accuracy can affect decisions about fairness and other values in certain domains, indicating that there are tradeoffs involved between privacy and accuracy, as well as between privacy and fairness.
